comments: Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition and remains near the center of the FOV for the entire test.  The flame oscillates for several cycles before radiatively extinguishing.  The LLUV flame diameter data has a lot of noise owing to the very dim flames combined with the contamination on the CIR LLUV viewing window.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/CO2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is almost motionless after deployment and ignition.  It then slowly drifts S and eventually out of the HiBMS FOV, but after flame extinction.  The flame appears to radially oscillate (primarily in intensity) a few seconds before extinction.  The droplet burns for about 15 sec and the flame appears weak but persists for quite a while.  Nice clean burn with no distortion or disruption.

comments: Free-floating methanol droplet in a 0.20/0.75.0.05 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The HiBMS IPSU failed to start and thus no droplet data was recorded.  The flame was bright and burned for over 5 seconds until a (presumed) diffusive extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of the HiBMS FOV shortly after visible flame extinction.  The color camera IPSU failed to record any images after droplet deployment.  The flame radiatively extinguishes and there is a vapor cloud visible on the downlink video some time after visible flame extinction.  This is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction following visible flame extinction.

Fber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There was no fiber translation on this test.  The droplet initially moves W in the HiBMS FOV before stopping and then slowly moving back to the center of the image.  There is a little disruption (maybe a small gas bubble popping) near flame extinction that is coincident with a small sattelite droplet being ejected from the droplet.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE at approximately 4 - 5 mm/sec  (deployment-induced, changed direction at ignition) and out of the HiBMS FOV after a few seconds.  The droplet remains in the LLUV and color camera FOVs for the entire test but is at the very edge of the FOVs of both cameras.  The flame gets continually dimmer throughout the test.  There is no extinction droplet diameter because the droplet is in the HiBMS FOV for such a small fraction of the burn.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.51/0.35 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet has a slow SE drift in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition.  The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV well after visible flame extinction, but then drifts back into the HiBMS FOV before the end of the recording period.  The droplet burned for a short time before flame extinction.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.13/0.87 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet oscillates transversely on fiber throughout the test.  It continues to move (relative to the fiber) even after the fiber stops translating.  It drifts out of the HiBMS FOV and to the edge of the LLUV FOV.  Only about half the test is captured by the HiBMS.  The color camera IPSU did not any images after deployment.  The extinction droplet diameter is based on extrapolating the droplet history using the measured burning rate constant while the droplet is within the HiBMS FOV (and extinction from the LLUV).

This is a freely-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.34/0.66 O2/N2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  This was the first successful test after switching from the high CO2, high pressure ambients where we had significant deployment problems.  The droplet has a high burning rate and stays in the HiBMS FOV the entire test.  Before flame extinction, the droplet distorts and eventually shatters coincident with flame extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N after deployment and ignition and out of the HiBMS FOV 1/3rd of the way through the burn.  The flame remains in the FOV of both the LLUV and color camera for the duration of the burn.  The flame is bright and very luminous from soot oxidation initially, but quickly becomes dimmer blue.  The luminosity increases slightly as the flame gets near extinction.  Because the droplet is out of the HiBMS FOV for the majority of the test, there is no extinction diameter reported.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NE in the HiBMS FOV, but stays in the FOV for the entire test.  Well after flame extinction, the droplet drifts partially out of the HiBMS FOV and then back in for the remainder of the recording time.  The flame grows continuously throughout the test getting dimmer until the flame extinguishes.  There is no evidence of a cool flame (continued vaporization or vapor cloud).

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient enviornment.  The droplet drifts NW in HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, but remains in the FOV for the entire burn, but leaves the FOV shortly after visible flame extinction.  The flame oscillates a few times before radiatively extinguishing.  There is a vapor cloud that forms approximately 20 seconds after visible flame extinction.  This is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction after visible flame extinction.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition, but then starts to drift SE in HiBMS FOV a few seconds after ignition.  The droplet drifts out of the HiBMS FOV, but remains in the LLUV and color camera FOVs.  The color camera IPSU failed to record any images after deployment.  The droplet burns for a relatively long time before a diffusive extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating the droplet history from the time the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until extinction using the burning rate constant from a short period just prior to the droplet leaving the HiBMS FOV.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There was no HiBMS data for this test.  There was poor alignment between the needle and the droplet and the droplet did not get deployed on the fiber.  It drifted N in the color camera FOV after deployment and ignition and out of the FOV before the end of the test.  The droplet stayed in the LLUV FOV the entire test.  The discrepancy in the flame size between the LLUV and color camera is because the flame is much brighter at the leading edge than the trailing edge and that results in a some of the flame being cropped from the color camera images during analysis.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There was significant oscillatory motion of the droplet on the fiber during the burn both before and after the translation.  The droplet swells and eventually disrupts before flame extinction leaving a small residual droplet on the fiber.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.15/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There was extra fuel dispensed after the automated sequence started.  The droplet drifts NW in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, hits the upper igniter and then quickly drifts SE and out of the HiBMS FOV.  The post deployment/ignition velocity is quite high, approximately 8 mm/sec.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.  It is unknown whether there was cool flame burning and extinction for this test.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.86 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet oscillates axially on the fiber throughout the flame lifetime, only becoming quiescient after visible flame extinction.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment with fiber translation after ignition.  An almost ideal fiber supported test with almost no oscillation of the droplet.  The fiber started and stopped moving with almost no relative motion imparted to the droplet.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  This is a smaller droplet that stays in the FOVs of all the cameras for the entire test.  The droplet burns to disruptive extinction at a small size.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet deploys and ignites with almost no residual motion and stays in the FOVs of all the cameras for the entire test.  The flame diffusively extinguishes

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.35/0.50 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment. It then drifts back into the HiBMS FOV before IPSU-1 recording stopped (thus the gap in the droplet history below).  This was a smaller droplet and a very short burn, likely outside quasi-steady flammability boundary, or more likely, right at the boundary.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  After ignition the droplet drifts NE and out of the HiBMS FOV.  The droplet remains out of the FOV until near the end of the test when it drifts back in from the NE corner.  The droplet drifts back in the FOV just before flame extinction.

Freely floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.37/0.66 O2/N2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition.  It drifts partially out of the FOV, but then drifts back in.  Ther is significant sooting with large agglomerates throughout the test.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.35/0.50 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet deploys with a relatively high (~ 6 mm/sec) NW drift velocity.  The burn time is relatively short and the droplet stays within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment. Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm (nominally air) ambient environment.  The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV for most of lifetime.  The droplet burns to a very small size, with a small disruption coincident with visible flame extinction.
Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in the FOVs of all the cameras for the entire burn.

Freely-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.30/0.70 O2/N2, 0.7 atm ambient envirronment.  The droplet drifts W in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of the FOV 2/3rds of the way through the test. Free-floating methanol droplet in a 0.14/0.86 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N after deployment and ignition, and out of HiBMS FOV.  Some time later it drifts back into the HiBMS FOV, just after visible flame extinction.  This is a weak flame with a long burn to diffusive extinction. Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a nominally air, 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, hits the igniter and begins to drift N. The flame oscillates briefly in the middle of the burn and then becomes steady and burns to a disruptive extinction.  The flame is very dim in the Color Camera FOV with the leading edge of the flame (in the direction of the droplet drift) much brighter than the trailing edge.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with no translation burning in a 0.18/0.82 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient.  The droplet remains stationary on the fiber and within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  The flame is very dim in both the LLUV and color camera views.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with 3 mm/sec translation (for approximately 4 seconds) burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There is very little axial or transverse oscillation on the fiber and the droplet stays within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  The visible flame extinguishes shortly after the fiber translation stops.  The droplet continues to vaporize at a relatively high rate after visible flame extinction and then there is some axial oscillation on the fiber, followed by a significant reduction in the vaporization rate.  The marked decrease in vaporization is coincident with a large vapor cloud formation with a torroidal vapor cloud in the immediate vicinity of the droplet.  This is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction following visible flame extinction.

Fiber-supported methanol with no translation burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test. There is little fiber glow after the droplet stops translating and from the flame measurements from the color camera, there are periodic oscillations of the flame size after the droplet stops translating.  The HiBMS IPSU stopped recording for a relatively large block of time just before igniter withdraw to about halfway through the burn.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts slowly E and then SE and out of the HiBMS FOV, but not until after flame extinction.  The flame oscillates significantly before extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a cabin air, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  This is the first FLEX test.  The droplet remains in the FOV of all of the cameras for the entire test.  The LLUV settings are not optimal and as a result the LLUV data are not reliable.  The droplet likely disrupted at the end of the test coincident with flame extinction.  The igniters were too bright and overexposed the HiBMS during ignition resulting in the inability to accurately measure the droplet diameter.

Freely-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.360/0.80 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S out of the HiBMS FOV about 1/3 the way through the test. Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, leaving the FOV when the visible flame extinguishes.  This was a large droplet and likely radiative extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet in a nominally air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm) ambient environment.  The droplet stays in the HiBMS FOV for the entire test including a long time after visible flame extinction.  The flame oscillates before visible flame extinction, apparent in both the LLUV and color camera views.  After flame extinction, the droplet vaporizes very vigorously with a nearly perfectly linear D^2 vs. time behavior.  The vaporization rate is only slightly lower than the burning rate constant before flame extinction.  The droplet vaporization rate then plateaus and this is coincident with the formation of a very large vapor cloud.  This behavior is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a cabin air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2), 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays within the FOV of all the cameras.  This is a 'calibration' run and the LLUV camera settings were not optimized.  As a result, the flame becomes undetectable in the LLUV midway through the burn.  The LLUV flame size for this test.  There is no evidence of disruptive burning near extinction.  The flame, however, seems to shrink quickly after ignition, maybe a small bubble burst.

Free-floating methanol droplet in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE in the HiBMS FOV after ignition and out of FOV right near diffusive extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter is extrapolated from the droplet history from the time the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until visible flame extinction using the burning rate constant from the last part of the burn while the droplet is within the FOV.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV and leaves the FOV about 2/3rds of the way through the burn.  The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating  the droplet history from the time the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until the time of flame extinction using the burning rate constant from the droplet history for a short period of time before the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.12/0.88 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV about 3/4ths of the way through the burn.  The flame is very dim, but does appear to grow, reach a maximum and then decrease in size in response to the shrinking droplet.  The extinction droplet diameter is based on extrapolating the droplet history to the time of extinction (as measured by the LLUV) using the burning rate constant measured from the last part of the droplet history while it is still in the HiBMS FOV.  This is likely diffusive extinction with a significant contribution from radiative loss.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.13/0.87 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N after deployment and ignition (deployment-induced motion) and out of the HiBMS FOV halfway through the test.  The flame stays within the LLUV and color camera FOVs the entire test.  The droplet burns for a long time in this ambient environment.  The extinction droplet diameter is based on extrapolating the droplet history using the measured burning rate constant while the droplet is within the HiBMS FOV.  The flame was very dim and the LLUV flame data is not as reliable because of the intensifier noise.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.19/0.71/0.10 O2/N2/CO2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV for the entire test, including a large period of time after visible flame extinction.  The droplet flame has a radiative extinction at a relatively large droplet size.  After visible flame extinction there is rapid and nearly constant vaporization of the droplet, followed by a vapor cloud formation and plateau in the droplet history.  The post visible-flame vaporization and plateau are indicative of cool flame burning and extinction, respectively.  The Color Camera IPSU-4 did not record any video after deployment.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.34/0.66 O2/N2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The HiBMS IPSU did not record any images for this test.  There appeared to be a possible needle fire.  The color camera and LLUV IPSUs stopped recording before the test was complete.  The LLUV images were recorded at 8-bit depth and no 12-bit which resulted in more uncertainty in the LLUV flame size measurements.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet had almost no residual motion after deployment and ignition and stayed in the HiBMS FOV for the entire time images were recorded.  The flame had a very short burn time, likely with radiative extinction.  There was a high vaporization rate after visible flame extinction, and an eventual plateau late in the HiBMS IPSU recording time coincident with a large vapor cloud.  The post visible flame extinction behavior is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.09/0.70 O2/N2/CO2, 3.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts E in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, hits the igniter and then drifts N.  The droplet immediately begins to grow disrupts and finally shatters that causes flame extinction.  This was likely due to a gas bubble trapped in the droplet after deployment.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.64/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition.  It drifts around the HiBMS FOV slightly and then disrupts coincident with flame extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter is the droplet diameter at disruption and not the true extinction droplet diameter.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with ~ 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.34/0.66 O2/N2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  After ignition and the start of translation, there is significnat transverse motion.  There is a lot of scatter in the droplet history because of the droplet motion on the fiber.  The flame view shows a bright flame with A LOT of sparklers throughout the burn.  The transverse droplet motion becomes more severe towards the end of the test, with the droplet deforming.  Flame extinction is coincident with a complete droplet disruption that tears the droplet off the fiber and extinguishes the flame.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with 3 mm/sec translation in a nominally air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2), 1 atm ambient.  There are moderate transverse oscillations on the fiber throughout the test.  There is unique circulation patterns in the gas phase evident from the soot motion.  The droplet continues to vaporize linearly after visible flame extinction and there is a large vapor cloud formed nearly coincident with a plateau in the droplet history.  This is evidence of cool flame burning and extinction following visible flame extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  Very little residual motion after deployment and ignition.  The droplet stays in the FOVs of all the cameras for the entire test.  The droplet burns cleanly to small size, then disrupts coincident with flame extinction.  The extinction droplet size is the droplet size when the flame/droplet disrupts.  The HiBMS IPSU (IPSU-1) stopped recording data sometime before deployment to partway through the burn.  The plotted data uses the first measured droplet as time zero although the droplet was burning for some time before that point.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.13/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  After deployment, there is some transverse, but no axial motion along fiber.  The transverse motion persists throughout the test, but stops after flame extinction.  There is no axial motion relative to the fiber, the droplet starts and stops with the start and stop of the fiber.  There is no disruption during this test.
Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a nominally air, 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in FOV of all cameras and diffusively extinguishes.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.09/0.70 O2/N2/CO2, 3.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet has a large drift NW in the HiBMS after deployment and ignition (ignition doesn't visually change the motion).  The droplet quickly drifts out of the FOV of the HiBMS.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images for this test.  The droplet also drifts N out of the LLUV FOV before extinction.  There is no burning rate or extinction droplet diameter listed because of the limited time the droplet is within the HiBMS FOV.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  A smaller droplet that drifts to the lower igniter after deployment.  The igniter seems to stop the drift and the droplet remains near the center of the FOV for the duration of the entire test.  The droplet burns to diffusive extinction.

Free-flaoating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.80 O2/N2 , 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet has almost no residual motion after ignition.  About 1/2 way though the test, the droplet begins to abruptly move NEE and then quickly changes direction to NE.  The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV after the second change in direction.  It appears from the color camera that there may be some small gas bubbles in the droplet.  There is also some distortion in the droplet history right before the droplet changes direction.  This could be due to the expanding gas bubbles distorting the droplet, then bursting and imparting a momentum to the droplet.  The burning rate constant and flame standoff data are for the portion of the test before the disruption and change in direction.  There is no extinction droplet diameter listed because of the limited time the droplet is in the HiBMS FOV and the disruptions in the droplet during the burn.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet (translated for approximately 3 sec. immediately after ignition) burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  This was a very clean test with very little droplet motion on the fiber.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with translation burning in a 0.34/0.66 O2/N2, 0.7 atm ambient.  The droplet burn is very smooth with little motion of the droplet relative to the fiber for most of the test.  About 80% of the way through the burn the droplet begins transverse vibrations on the fiber.  The vibrations grow in magnitude until the droplet disrupts and disintegrates, extinguishing the flame and leaving no fuel droplet on the fiber.  The LLUV IPSU stopped recording for about 1/2 of the test (in the middle).

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N after deployment and ignition and out of HiBMS FOV about 1/4th of the way through the burn.  The drift velocity is relatively high and the flame is brighter on the leading edge in the direction of the drift.  The droplet does stay in the FOV of both the LLUV and Color cameras.  There is no extinction diameter for this test because it was in the HiBMS FOV for such a small fraction of the burn.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment for this test.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts E after deployment and ignition and  out of HiBMS FOV before extinction.  It then drifts briefly back in the HiBMS FOV immediately after flame extinction.  The color camera IPSUdid not record any images after deployment.  The droplet drifted partially out of the LLUV FOV for a portion of the burn (resulting in more scatter in the flame size measurement).  The extinction droplet diameter is estimated by interpolating the droplet history with a cubic polynomial from the known and measured droplet size and burning rate in the segments of the droplet history just before it left the HiBMS FOV and after it re-entered the FOV.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.13/0.87 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  Droplet stays in HiBMS FOV for most of the test.  For a short period of time, right around visible flame extinction, the droplet drifts partially out of the FOV.  It drifts back into the HiBMS FOV for the remainder of the HiBMS IPSU-1 recording time.  The flame is very dim, barely obove the background level in both the LLUV and color Cameras.  The extinction droplet diameter results from interpolating the droplet history from when the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV to when it re-enters a short time after visible flame extinction.  The interpolation polynomial is a fourth order polynomial with the constraint that the values and burning rate constants at both ends match the experimental values.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N after deployment and ignition and out of the HiBMS FOV about 1/3rd of the way through the test.  The color camera IPSU-4 did not record any images after deployment.  The droplet burns to diffusive extinction without disruption.  There is no extinction droplet diameter reported since the droplet was within the HiBMS FOV for such a short fraction of the burn time.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N slowly, the turns S and drifts slowly before accelerating out of the FOV right after visible flame extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stayed in the HiBMS FOV the entire test.  The LLUV provided good distortion free and bright images.  The flame radiatively extinguished.  The visible flame extinction was followed by rapid vaporization, then plateau when the droplet became quite small.  There was a visible vapor cloud formation late in the recording history.  The post visible flame extinction behavior is consistent with cool flame burning and extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.35/0.50 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet has a very small S drift after deployment and ignition, but remains in the HiBMS FOV for the entire recording time.  Very short burn, with the droplet being either significantly larger than the radiative extinction limit or completely outside the quasi-steady flammability boundary.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with 3 mm/sec translation (for approximately 4 seconds) burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There is only a little axial and transverse oscillation after deployment and ignition and druing translation of the fiber, but for most of the burn and post-burn, the droplet is relatively quiescent.  The droplet remains in the HiBMS FOV for the entire recording duration of HiBMS IPSU-1.  The flame radiatively extinguishes, preferentially along the fiber axis.  The droplet continues to vaporize at a high rate after visible flame extinction.  The vaporization then slows considerably and there is a visible vapor cloud formed.  This is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction following visible flame extinction.

Free floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.09/0.70 O2/N2/CO2, 3.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet quickly drifts N and out of the HiBMS FOV after ignition.  The burning rate constant is not listed since there is in the HiBMS FOV for such a short time.  The droplet does not drift out of the FOV of the LLUV, but the IPSU data for the LLUV ends before the flame extinguishes.  The droplet drifts NE and out of the Color Camera FOV before the flame extinguishes.  The flame from the color camera view is visibly brighter in the direction of the translation, an indication that the convective motion is significantly impacting the flame behavior.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.15/0.64 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts E in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of the FOV right before diffusive extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating the droplet history from the time it leaves the FOV until visible flame extinction using the measured burning rate constant from the last part of the burn.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.19/0.71/0.10 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient enviornment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV and leaves the FOV immediately after visible flame extinction.  It remains in the FOV of all the cameras for the entire burn that ends with diffusive extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  Excellent deployment with almost no residual motion after deployment and ignition.  The droplet drifts a little S in the HiBMS FOV but stays in the FOV of all cameras for the entire test.  The droplet burns cleanly down to a small size where it disrupts coincident with flame extinction.  The extinction droplet size is the droplet size when the disruption occurs.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.50/0.36 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains in the FOV of all cameras.  This is a short burn to radiative extinction.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SSE and out of the HiBMS FOV before the end of the test.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images for this test.  The LLUV shows a very long burn with a flame that appears to get a little bit brighter for a short period of time.  There is no extinction droplet diameter listed because the droplet is out of the HiBMS FOV for most of the droplet lifetime.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.19/0.59/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays with the FOV of all the cameras for the entire burn.  The flame diffusively extinguishes.  The LLUV images are dim, but the flame size data seems reasonable, but it is a bit noisy.  This is the result of both the dim LLUV images and the contamination of the CIR LLUV viewing window.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains in the HiBMS FOV (and the FOV of all the cameras) for the entire test.  The flame grows throughout the test and gets dimmer until radiatively extinguishing after approximately 5 seconds.  There appears to be no evidence of cool flame formation (no rapid vaporization after visible flame extinction and no vapor cloud formed in the color camera view).

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is almost motionless after deployment and ignition.  This is a large droplet and stays in HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  The flame grows and continually gets dimmer after ignition and quickly extinguishes due to radiative loss.  After visible flame extinction, the droplet continues vaporize at almost the same rate until a plateau well after flame extinction.  The plateau is coincident with the formation of a large vapor cloud.  Both are indicative of cool flame burning and extinction after visible flame extinction.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.64/0.16 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition.  The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV 3/4ths of the way through the burn and then back into the FOV just after visible flame extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter is the droplet diameter when the droplet fully re-appears in the FOV and should be nearly identical to the droplet diameter when the visible flame extinguishes.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in the FOVs of all that cameras for the entire burn.  The droplet burnis for a short time to likely radiative extinction.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with fiber translation burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet does not oscillate much on the fiber during or after the burn.  There is s small vapor cloud formed after visible flame extinction.  It is difficult to determine whether there was cool flame burning and extinction from the available data.  The LLUV IPSU did not record any images during the burn.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.20/0.80 O2/N2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There is moderate transverse and axial oscillations on the fiber after deployment and during the entire visible flame and after visible flame extinction.  The flame extinguishes after the translation stops, with the trailing edge of the flame visibly weaker and extinguishing first.  There are unusual, recirculating flow patterns in the HiBMS fuel from soot that moves toward the droplet, accelerates circuferentially a short arc and then goes radially towards the flame and back again.  There is a small vapor cloud formed in the color camera view approximately 20 sec after visible flame extinction.  It is not clear if cool flame burning and extinction was present in this test.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet migrates slowly W in the HiBMS FOV after ignition but remains in the FOV the entire test.  There is a small spot on fiber that burns off early in burn.  A short burn to extinction.  This is near the LOI in this ambient mixture.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in the FOVs of all the cameras for the very short burn and for a considerable period of time after visible flame extinction.  The LLUV stopped recording images for several seconds right around ignition.  This was a very short burn with no appreciable vaporization or vapor cloud formation after visible flame extinction.  There was likely no cool flame or only a very brief cool flame.

Free-floating heptane droplet in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV with very little residual motion for the entire test.  The flame radiative extinguishes quickly, followed by rapid vaporization and then by a large vapor cloud formation.  This means that cool flame burning and extinction following visible flame extinction was likely.  The HiBMS FOV view dims when cloud forms and this is likely the cause of the dropelt getting slightly larger at the end of the test (the changing background combined with the fixed segmentation value caused more pixels to be counted as 'droplet').

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a cabin air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2), 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains within the FOV of all the cameras.  This was a 'calibration' run using cabin air and the LLUV setting was not optimal as the flame was very difficult to see and measure (especially near the end of the test).

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.16/0.84 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition and stays in FOV of all cameras throughout the entire recording time of the IPSUs.  The flame grows, radiatively extinguishes and then there is rapid post-visible flame extinction vaporization.  The vaporization rate of the droplet actually increases after visible flame extinction and then rapidly decreases coincident with vapor cloud formation.  The behavior after visible flame extinction is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of FOV, but well after extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.25/0.60/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet slowly drifts E in the HiBMS FOV and out of the FOV before the test ends.  Just as the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV, the liquid starts to oscillate slightly; the motion is visible in the color camera view.  The flame extinguishes abruptly, and is likely due to disruption.

Freely-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts slighly N and then E in the HiBMS FOV.  It evenutally leaves the HiBMS FOV, but well after extinction.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment for this test.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains within the FOV of all cameras and burns to diffusive extinction.  The LLUV data has a lot of noise associated with the very dim flame and the smudge on the CIR LLUV viewing window.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a cabin air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2), 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is misshapen on the neddles before the stretch and deploy.  Ignition imparts a significant drift velocity on the droplet to the E.  This could be due to a small air bubble that distorted the droplet and then popped when the igniters turned on.  The droplet drifts out of the HiBMS FOV and then drifts back in the FOV.  The flame extinguishes without disruption.  This is a 'calibration' test in cabin air.  The flame image in not discernable in the LLUV view late in the flame lifetime because the LLUV settings were not optimized for these tests.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, goes to the end of the FOV, then drifts W briefly and then back N, never leaving the FOV of any of the cameras.  The flame diffusively extinguishes.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N after deployment and ignition, then begins to drift back to the center.  It stays in the HiBMS FOV until 4/5 of the way through the burn when the HiBMS stops recording data for about 5 seconds.  The HiBMS did not record data when the flame extinguished.  It was a long burn, with the extinction diameter estimated from the droplet history extrapolated until visible flame extinction using the measured burning rate constant for a short time right before recording stopped.

Free-floating heptane droplet in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There were problems with gas bubbles during the dispense/stretch/deployment.  On this test there was a small gas bubble that burst during ignition and caused the droplet to oscillate.  The droplet drifts slowly SSE and out of the HiBMS FOV a few seconds after radiative extinction.  The droplet continues to vaporize at a relatively high rate after flame extinction although there are only a few seconds before the droplet left the HiBMS FOV.  There is a vapor cloud that forms 10 - 20 seconds after visible flame extinction.  The post visible flame extinction behavior is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.16/0.84 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient evnironment.  The droplet drifts N in the color camera FOV.  The HiBMS IPSU did not record any images for this test.  The droplet stayed in the FOV of the LLUV and color camera.  The flame burns for a short time to radiative extinction.  This is likely followed by cool flame burning and extinction.  The color camera shows a large vapor cloud formed some time after visible flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.12/0.88 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The HiBMS IPSU did not record any images for this test.  The droplet does not drift after deployment and ignition and stays in the FOVs of both the LLUV and color cameras.  The flame is very dim and almost undetectable by the LLUV (especially later in the flame lifetime).  As a result, the LLUV flame size measurements for the last half of the test are not accurate (the flame essentially undetectable by the LLUV).

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a nominally air, 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE after deployment, does not touch the igniter and continues to drift SE in the HiBMS FOV.  The droplet drifts S and out of LLUV FOV.  IPSU4 did not record color camera data and it is unclear whether disruption occurred.  There is no extinction droplet diameter reported because of the small fraction of the total test that the droplet is within the HiBMS FOV.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts E after deployment and ignition in the HiBMS FOV leaving the FOV just prior to extinction or burnout.  The droplet burns to a very small size and then appears to disrupt or rapidly change direction after the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV.  The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating the droplet history from the time it leaves the FOV until flame extinction using the measured burning rate constant.  The small extinction droplet size suggests that the droplet burned almost to completion.

Freely-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.30/0.70 O2/N2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of the FOV after approximately 2/3 of the burn is complete.  There is a bright luminous flame that persists throughout the droplet lifetime.  There is significant sooting with large soot agglomerates present throughout the burn.  There is a disruption that is coincident with flame extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient envrionment.  The droplet drifts out of HiBMS FOV (but remains in the FOV of the LLUV and Color Camera) close to extinction.  There is a small vapor cloud formed at extinction.  There is noise in the analysis of the droplet image because of soot particles formed during combustion that interfere with the analysis.  It is unclear whether this is radiative or diffusive extinction or if there was a cool flame after visible flame extinction.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.63/0.20 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  This is a smaller droplet.  After ignition there is a lot of motion on the fiber, not really disruptive burning where the droplet becomes dislodged from the fiber, but the motion clearly influences the burning history.  The droplet burned to completion.  The color camera did not record to the on-board IPSU for this test.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.54/0.32 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains in the FOV of all the cameras for the entire burn.  The flame oscillates for several cycles of increasing magnitude before radiatively extinguishing.  The LLUV images are dim and the the LLUV flame data has a lot of noise as a result of the dimness of the flames and the contamination on the CIR LLUV viewing window.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts slowly E along the fiber in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition.  There is a little disruptive motion on the fiber during the burning history.  This is a diffusive extinction.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet ignites and shortly after ignition a small droplet or debris ignites to the W (color camera) or N (LLUV) of the droplet.  This small droplet/particle burns for only a short time.  It is not visible in the HiBMS.  The droplet burns for only a short time before radiatively extinguishing.  There is continued rapid vaporization after visible flame exinction, followed by avapor cloud formation approximately 5 seconds after visible flame extinction.  This is an indication of cool flame burning and extinction following visible flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.09/0.70 O2/N2/CO2, 3.0 atm ambient environment (the actual ambient is different because of the issues with the CIR adsorber loop).  The droplet drifts W in the HiBMS FOV, hits the igniter and drifts SE after igniter withdraw, leaving the FOV and then reapperaing for a short time before disappearing again.  The glow from the igniter influences the droplet size measurement early, the HiBMS and illumination package settings not quite good enough although better than on the earlier tests.  The extinction droplet diameter is not listed because the droplet was not in the HiBMS FOV for enough of the test.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet has oscillations on the fiber throughout the burn, but remains in the HiBMS FOV.  Large soot agglomerates interfere with the droplet size measurement for a portion of the burn.  The flame radiatively extinguishes after a very long, slow, high amplitude oscillation.  This is followed by rapid vaporization with vapor cloud coincident with the plateau.  The droplet moves during the vaporization but it doesn't seem to inpact the size measurement significantly.  There is a small disruption near the end of the vaporization and a small jump in droplet size, maybe a gas bubble that bursts.  There was likely a cool flame and cool flame extinction following the visible flame extinction.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.30/0.70 O2/N2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is relatively heavily sooting immediately after ignition.  Shortly after ignition the droplet begins to severely distort, periodically expelling small droplets of fuel that continue to burn.  There is a large disruption that completely dislodges the droplet from the fiber.  This droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV, then S (after another disruption) and then burns relatively cleanly to disruption at a small size.  The burning rate constant is that during the relatively clean period after the droplet gets dislodged from the fiber.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NE after ignition, but slowly and remains in the FOV for the entire test.  The droplet is initially luminous with a bight yellow flame that eventually turns blue with a little yellow and then blue until the end of the test.  The droplet burns to a small size before a small disruption coincident with flame extinction.  The LLUV IPSU-2 stopped recording for about 7 seconds in the middle of the test.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.30/0.70 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There is some transverse motion after deployment that persists throughout the test.  There is also significant oscillatory axial motion during the translation that persists after the fiber stops translating.  The droplet drifts axially out of the HiBMS FOV about 1/3rd of the way through the burn.  There is significant 'sparkling' evident in the color camera view.  It is not visible in either the HiBMS or LLUV.  The droplet disrupts and becomes dislodged from the fiber coincident with flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.54/0.32 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, leaving the droplet shortly after visible flame extinction and then back into the FOV well after extinction near the end of recording.  This is a very dim flame with the LLUV data having a lot of noise because of the dimness and the contamination on the CIR LLUV viewing window.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.136/0.50/0.363 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts W in the HiBMS FOV after deployment hits the igniter and then drifts slowly E after ignition.  It leaves the HIBMS FOV shortly after visible flame extinction.  The LLUV images are very dim which when combined with the contamination on the CIR LLUV viewing window results in a lot of noise in the data.  This flame oscillates for nearly half the lifetime.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts E and out of HiBMS FOV.  After drifting out of the HiBMS FOV, it drifts back in slightly, then out again for good.  Diffusive extinction after long burn.  There is no extinction diameter listed for this test because the droplet was in the HiBMS FOV for only a small fraction of the total test.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a high 0.21/0.09/0.70 O2/N2/CO2, 3.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts and hits the igniter before igniter withdraw and drifts slowly W in the HiBMS FOV, but stays in the FOVs of all the cameras for the entire test.  There was significant translation in the HiBMS FOV during the test.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains in the HiBMS FOV but there is a lot of motion on the fiber and eventually the droplet disrupts and becomes dislodged from the fiber.  There is no extinction droplet diameter reported as a result of the disruption.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.21/0.49/0.30, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet moves axially on the fiber a short distance after translation stops and partially out of the HiBMS FOV.  By the end of the HiBMS IPSU-1 recording it moves completely back into the HiBMS FOV.  There is a small droplet or debris on the fiber that ignites and briefly burns (burns out) before the flame extinguishes.  The flame radiatively extinguishes before translation stops.  The droplet continues to vaporize at a relatively high rate and the vaporization rate slows which is coincident with a visible vapor cloud forming.  The vapor cloud forms a torroidal ring around the droplet and the background intensity in the HiBMS decreases significantly as the vapor cloud forms.  The post visible flame extinction behavior is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a nominally air, 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE after deployment and into the igniter, changes direction to N after igniter withdraw.  The droplet drifts N during the burn and out of HiBMS FOV.  The flame grows, remains stable (no oscillations) and then shrinks to a disruptive extinction at a relatively small size.  The droplet remained in the LLUV for the entire test.  The MDCA Color Camera did not record images on-board for this test (the downlinked video is available).

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV (and the FOV of all cameras) for the entire test.  The flame grows continusously after ignition, radiatively extinguishing after approximately 5 seconds.  Ther appears to be no cool flame or only a very brief one (no significant vaporization after extinction and also no vapor cloud formation in the color camera view).

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.54/0.32 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition and remains within the FOV of all the cameras for the duration of the test.  The flame oscillates for several seconds with increasing magnitude before radiatively extinguishing.  The LLUV images are dim and the LLUV flame data has a lot of noise because of the dimness of the flame and the contamination on the CIR LLUV viewing window.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.16/0.84 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in FOV of all cameras for the entire IPSU recording time.  The flame grows and exhibits radiative extinction shortly after ignition.  There is then a period of rapid post-extinction vaporization followed by a plateau in the droplet history coincident with the appearance of a vapor cloud.  Both are indicative of cool flame burning and extinction following visible flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.16/0.59/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition and stays within the FOV of all cameras for the entire burn.  A long burn to diffusive extinction.  The LLUV images are dim and there is a lot of noise in the LLUV flame size data owing to both the dimness of the flame and the contamination of the CIR LLUV viewing window.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a cabin air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2), 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains within the FOV of all the cameras and burns to diffusive extinction.  This was a 'calibration' run and the LLUV setting was not optimal and as a result the LLUV flame data is not reliable especially near the end of the test.  The droplet does not disrupt, but there is clearly something that happens to the flame near the end of the test.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts slowly NE in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of the FOV a little over half way through the test.  The droplet burns to a small size and then disrupts.  Extrapolating the droplet history to the time of extinction shows that the droplet had almost completely vaporized when it disrupted ending the test.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Freely-floating methanol droplet burning in a nominally air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm) ambient environment.  The droplet is almost motionless after deployment and ignition.  It slowly starts drifting N in the HiBMS FOV, then starts moving N much quicker and out of the HiBMS FOV about 1/2 way through the test.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images for this test.  It is unclear from the LLUV whether the droplet disrupted coincident with flame extinction.  There is no extinction droplet diameter listed since the droplet was out of the HiBMS FOV for such a long time near visible flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in the HiBMS and LLUV FOVs for entire test.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.  The flame diffusively extinguished with no disruption.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.30/0.70 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains in the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  There is some axial and transverse droplet motion from deployment until the end of the test.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.  The extinction droplet diameter is the droplet diameter when the droplet disrupts and becomes dislodged from the fiber.  The disruption is coincident with flame extinction.  There is some droplet swelling or shape change before disruption.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.30/0.70 O2/N2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet exhibits significant axial oscillations during and after the start and stop of fiber translation.  The droplet drifts in and partially out of the HiBMS FOV.  At the end of the test, the droplet swells, disrupts and becomes dislodged from the fiber.  The disruption is coincident with flame extinction (the dislodged droplet does burn as it drifts away).  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Free-floating heptane droplet in a 0.21/.0.49/0.30 O2/N2/He, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  The flame grows to a maximum size shortly after ignition and then stays at a constant size until flame extinction.  It is unclear whether this is diffusive or radiative extinction.  There is no evidence of prolonged cool flame burning after visible flame extinction (no rapid vaporization after or vapor cloud formation in the color camera).

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.13/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  Very short burn that is entirely transient.  This ambient is likely below the quasi-steady flammability limit.  There is a small vapor cloud that forms shortly after visible flame extinction.  This may be indicative of cool flame burning and extinction following hot flame extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.63/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There is almost no drift in the HiBMS FOVand the droplet remains in the FOVs of all cameras for the entire recording time.  The flame radiatively extinguishes quickly after ignition.  There vaporization rate increases after visible flame extinction and then quickly plateaus well after visible flame extinction, indicative of cool flame burning and extinction.  The HiBMS view gets extremely dark coincident with the vapor cloud formation.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There was very little droplet motion after deployment and ignition (it only moved a few mm during the entire test).

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation in a 0.25/0.60/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There are moderate axial oscillations on the fiber (lower frequency than some of the tests with severe oscillations) while the droplet is translating.  The oscillations stop and the droplet burns nicely until the end of the test when there is a disruption coincident with flame extinction.  The increase in droplet size at the end of the test is likely the result of bubble nucleation and growth.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet does not drift at all in any of the camera FOVs after deployment and ignition.  The flame oscillates a few times before radiatively extinguishing.  The color camera flame data is more reliable in this test as it was easier to distinguish the flame boundaries.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.13/0.47/0.40 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV for the entire recording period.  Very short burn to extinction.  This is likely below the flammability limit.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  There is almost no drift and the droplet remains in HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  The HiBMS recording stops before burn is complete and the droplet drifted out of the LLUV FOV before the end of the test.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.15/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet has very little residual motion after deployment and ignition with only a very small drift N in the HiBMS FOV.  The droplet stays in FOV of all cameras throughout the recording time of the IPSUs.  The flame grows and gets dimmer after ignition and radiatively extinguishes shortly after ignition.  This is followed by a period of rapid vaporization and then a quick plateau in the droplet history coincident with the formation of a vapor cloud.  Both of these are evidence of cool flame burning and extinction after visible flame extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.27/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N after deployment and ignition and out of the HiBMS FOV shortly after visible flame extinction.  Some time after visible flame extinction there is a large vapor cloud of (presumable) formed.  This is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction following visible flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.13/0.87 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts E then S and out of the SE corner of the HiBMS FOV just after visible flame extinction.  The flame oscillates for several seconds before radiative extinction.  The flame is very difficult to discern in the LLUV view.  The flame luminosity barely registers on the LLUV.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images for this test.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.15/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  This is a very small droplet, smaller than would be typically recommended to burn in the apparatus.  The droplet drifts NNW in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition with a significant (7 - 8 mm/sec) velocity and leaves the FOV before the test is complete.  The droplet burns to completion without disruption with a dim blue flame and only a little luminous region after ignition.

This is a freely deployed methanol droplet burning in cabin air.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition leaving the HiBMS FOV 1/3rd of the way through the burn.  There is some evidence of flame disruption prior to extinction, but it is difficult to judge from the color camera images.  This was a 'calibration' test point.  The igniter overwhelmed the HiBMS and made measuring the droplet impossible until the igniters withdrew.  The LLUV setting was not optimal and the flame nearly disappeared from the LLUV 1/2 way through the burn coincident to when there is a noticeable change in the flame behavior in the Color Camera.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NE and out of the HiBMS FOV about 1/4 of the way through the burn.  The droplet burned for a very long time.  The flame was very dim and difficult to see, with significant noise in the LLUV using automated analysis and a very low threshold for manual analysis.  The droplet starts to oscillate in the midway point of the burn for a few seconds, then burns with a steady flame until it oscillates again right before flame extinction.  There is no extinction droplet diameter listed because the droplet is in the HiBMS FOV for such a short time.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  This is very small heptane droplet.  It drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, but stays in the FOV the entire recording time.  The droplet burns with a relatively bright flame to a very small size where there is a small disruption that is coincident with visible flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NW in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, hits the igniter and then drifts quickly S after ignition.  The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV shortly after ignition so only a small portion of the droplet burning history is captured.  It also leaves the color camera FOV.  Because only a short part of the burning history is captured, there is no extinction droplet diameter listed and the burning rate constant is likely inaccurate.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.82 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains in the HiBMS FOV the entire test, drifting N after deployment, stopping, drifting SW to the corner of the FOV and then N to the middle W of the FOV.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images for this test.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm (nominally air) ambient environment.  The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV (it briefly drifts out well after visible flame extinction) for the entire test.  This test likely had a cool flame following visible flame extinction.  There was a large vapor cloud formed at the end of the test.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.35/0.50 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts slowly S but remains in the HiBMS FOV for the entire test and well after flame extinction.  The droplet abruptly leaves the HiBMS FOV in the video, likely because the HiBMS stopped archiving images for a short time.  Very short burn, either radiative extinction or outside the quasi-steady flammability boundary all together.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There was no fiber translation.  Large droplet appears to radiatively extinguish.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.  The LLUV IPSU lost data for about 5 sec during the test.  The LLUV images are very dim and it was almost impossible to detect the edges of the flame.  The flame appeared on the LLUV view to be quenched where the flame and fiber met.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient enviornment.  The droplet drifts NW after deployment in the HiBMS FOV, hits the igniter and then drifts SE after ignition and out of the FOV approximately 8 sec after igniter withdraw.  The droplet burns with a very weak relatively steady flame for a long period of time before oscillating before extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter is based on extrapolating the droplet history to the time of extinction using the measured burning rate constant from just before when the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet moves W along the fiber a short distance after deployment and ignition but before translation and then moves E with the fiber during translation.  The droplet remains within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  There is very little motion of the droplet relative to the fiber during the test.  There is a small disruption coincindent with flame extinction that leaves a slightly smaller droplet on the fiber.  The extinction droplet diameter is the droplet diameter just prior to the diruption.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.63 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  Neither the HiBMS or color camera IPSUs recorded any images for this test.  The droplet burns for a short time to disruption.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.25/0.60/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet deploys and ignites with almost no residual motion.  It stays within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  The droplet burns cleanly with a brighter blue flame the entire test.  Near the end of test, there is droplet deformation (becoming football shaped), and then disruption that is coincident with flame extinction.  The droplet shatters at the end of the test.  The end of the test is likely compromised by the conformal coating needle contamination.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, to the edge of the FOV, then E and out of HiBMS FOV before end of test.  The flame 'swirls' a little before extinction in both LLUV and color camera.  The droplet was not in the HiBMS FOV long enough to get an accurate estimate of the extinction droplet diameter.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition, drifts around the HiBMS FOV, but remains in the FOV for the entire burn and well after visible flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.17/0.63/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deploment and ignition, stays in the FOV, briefly drifts N, then E and out of the HiBMS FOV just prior to visible (diffusive) flame extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating the droplet history until the time of flame extinction (from the LLUV) using the measured burning rate constant from the later part of the burn.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a nominally air, 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stayed in the FOVs of all cameras for the entire burn, but did drift S and out of the HiBMS FOV shortly after diffusive extinction.  IPSU1 did not record every frame.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in the HiBMS FOV (and the FOV of all the cameras) for the entire test.  The flame grows, reaches a maximum size and then decreases in size until diffusive extinction at a very small size.  Shortly after extinction, the droplet appears to disrupt and disappears from the HiBMS FOV.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.13/0.87 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The HiBMS IPSU did not record any images and the color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.  This was a very short burn with almost no burning after igniter withdraw.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet has a high drift velocity to the N after deployment.  The droplet hits the igniter and then continues to move NNW after ignition at approx 7 - 8 mm/sec.  It leaves the HiBMS FOV relatively quickly and well before flame extinction.  There is no extinction droplet diameter listed since the droplet was out of the HiBMS FOV for most of the burn.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment for this test.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.13/0.87 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The HiBMS IPSU did not record any images for this test.  This was a very short flame lifetime with the flame extinguishing before the droplet started translating.  There was a small vapor cloud formed some time after visible flame extinction.  It is unclear whether there was cool flame burning and extinction following visible flame extinction.

Fiber-supported methanol with no translation burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  The flame then becomes very dim blue and is nearly cylindrical because of the flame quenching due to the support fiber.  There is little fiber glow after the droplet stops translating and from the flame measurements from the color camera, there are periodic oscillations of the flame size after the droplet stops translating.  The HiBMS IPSU stopped recording for a relatively large block of time just before igniter withdraw to about halfway through the burn.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.64/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of HiBMS FOV about 1/2 way through the burn.  The droplet then drifts back in shortly after diffusive extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter results from a cubic polynomial fit of the droplet history between the two times that the droplet is within the HiBMS FOV (subject to the constraint that the slope of the droplet history of the fit is equal to that of the experiment just before it leaves and after it returns to the FOV).

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition.  Midway through the burn the droplet drifts S and leaves the HiBMS FOV just before the flame extinguishes.  The droplet remains in the FOVs of the LLUV and color cameras.  The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating the droplet history from the time the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until the time of flame extinction using the burning rate constant measured near the end of the time when the droplet is within the HiBMS FOV.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a nominally air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2), 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts E out of the HiBMS FOV about 1/2 the way through the test.  The flame oscillates for several seconds before leaving the FOV of all the cameras.  It leaves the LLUV FOV last, and is oscillating as it translates S out of the FOV.  The radiometer shows flame persists even after leaving the FOV.  Extrapolating the burning history to when the radiometer indicates extinction (with large error bars) shows that the droplet burns nearly to extinction.  There is no evidence of disruptive burning in any of the camera views.  The color camera did not zoom out so it did not capture the flame history correctly.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There is a small residue on the fiber to the W of the droplet that ignites a few sec after droplet ignition.  This residue burns for 1 - 2 sec with a very bright luminous flame (during translation).  The droplet drifts partially out of the HiBMS FOV after the translation stops, then shrinks back to be completely in the FOV.  There appears to be some oscillations near extinction.  The droplet burns without transverse or axial oscillations along the fiber.  There is no disruption or droplet deformation.

Freely-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.30/0.70 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  Significant sooting with large agglomerates throughout the test.  A very luminous flame that persists throughout the droplet lifetime until disruptive extinction.  The droplet drifts NW out of the HiBMS FOV 1/3rd of the way through the test.  It remains in the LLUV and color camera FOVs the entire test.  The degree of sooting made accurate measurement of the droplet size difficult.

Freely deployed heptane droplet burning in a cabin air (nominally 0.21/0.79 O2/N2), 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE out of the HiBMS FOV a few seconds after igniter withdraw.  Significant sooting is apparent in the HiBMS.  The droplet also drifts out of the color camera FOV.  It remains in the LLUV FOV for the entire burn.  There is a lot of noise in the droplet diameter data because of the soot.  The droplet disrupts at the end of the burn (from the LLUV).

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.09/0.70 O2/N2/CO2, 3.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE after deployment, hits the igniter, changes direction and quickly moves W out of HiBMS FOV as well as LLUV and color camera FOVs.  The HiBMS produced a saturated image that influences the droplet size measurement.  The HiBMS backlight was also too strong and the droplet size measurement was a function on which 'quad-slice' of the HiBMS image the droplet was in.  There is no burning rate constant and extinction droplet diameter listed because of the short time the droplet was in the HiBMS FOV.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts E out of HiBMS FOV just before radiative extinction.  There is a large vapor cloud formed 15 - 20 seconds after visible flame extinction (visible in the color camera.  The vapor cloud means that cool flame burning and extinction after visible flame extinction was likely.  The extinction droplet diameter is extrapolated from the droplet history using the measured burning rate constant (later in the droplet lifetime) and the time of extinction from the LLUV.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with no translation in a 0.25/0.60/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There is significant axial and transverse oscillations on the fiber after ignition.  While the droplet is oscillating on the fiber, there are 'sparklers' evident on the color camera view.  The oscillations diminish and the droplet burns cleanly (on the color camera view as well). A few seconds before there is a disruption (without dislocation) and then a complete disruption/dislocation/flame extinction.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.20/0.80 O2/N2, 0.7 atm ambient.  The droplet remains in the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  After the start of translation, the droplet oscillates rapidly between where the flame impinges on the fiber.  The oscillation stops at approximately halfway through the test.  The periodic noise in the droplet history is caused by the oscillation.  The droplet then grows and has a small disruption leaving a small residual droplet on the fiber.  The burst or disruption is coincident with flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.16/0.59/0.25 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition and remains in the FOV of all the cameras for the entire recording time.
