It is difficult to say whether this is diffusive or radiative extinction.  It is likely near the flammability boundary.  The MDCA Color Camera did not record anything beyond droplet deployment on-board for this test.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.19/0.71/0.10 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts E and then SE and out of the HiBMS FOV about 1/3 of the way through the test.  This was a very long burn with likely diffusive extinction.  There was no disruption at extinction.  There is no extinction droplet diameter reported because the droplet was in the HiBMS FOV for only a small fraction of the entire burn.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.82 O2/N2 ambient, 1.0 atm ambient.  The droplet slowly drifts E out of the HiBMS FOV accelerating slowly before leaving the FOV.  The droplet remains in the LLUV and color camera FOVs for the entire test.  There is no disruption.  There is no extinction droplet diameter listed because the droplet is not in the HiBMS FOV for the majority of the burning history.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There is a lot of transverse and axial oscillatory motion during the entire droplet burn.  The droplet does not leave the HiBMS FOV during the test, but the burning rate is high which is likely the result of the significant and high frequency oscillations.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with 3 mm/sec translation in a nominally air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2), 1 atm ambient.  The HiBMS IPSU stopped recording for a few seconds which resulted in a gap in the droplet history.  The droplet oscillates on the fiber throughout the test, with the amplitude and frequency changing.  There is also some unusual gas-phase recirculation evident from soot particle motion.  The droplet vaporizes vigorously after visible flame extinction.  There is also a large vapor cloud formed near the end of the recording period.  This is evidence of cool flame burning and extinction following visible flame extinction.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a nominally air (0.21/0.79 O2/N2), 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains in the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  There is significant oscillatory axial motion during the most of the test.  At the very end, the droplet does become stationary.  There is some deformation/growth/shape change at the end of the test.  There is a small disruption that is coincident with flame extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.16/0.59/0.25 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  This is a smaller droplet that is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition.  It stays in the FOV of all the cameras.  The flame surrounding the droplet extinguishes at a very small size, near the limit of what we can reasonably measure.  The flame size is nearly constant throughout the burn, decreasing only slightly towards the end of the burn after only slightly increasing in size initially.  The flame standoff increases linearly throughout the burn.

Freely-floating methanol droplet droplet burning in a 0.34/0.66 O2/N2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in the HiBMS FOV for the entire test and drifts slowly SSE during the test.  The droplet begins to change shape, becomes almost oblong with a pointed end (from the video) before disrupting.  The disruption is coincident with flame extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.14/0.86 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  This is a small droplet that drifts quickly NW in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of the FOV a short time after igniter withdraw.  The droplet appears to radiatively extinguish, even at this relatively small size.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NE in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, but remains in the FOV of all cameras for the entire test.  The droplet burns for several seconds, the flame grows, reaches a maximum size and remains nearly constant for the entire test.  The luminosity of the flame continuously decreases as the droplet burns.  This is likely near the flammability limit.  There is no evidence of cool flame formation (no rapid vaporization or vapor cloud formation).

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NW in the HiBMS view after deployment, then hits the igniter and moves in the NE direction and out of the HiBMS FOV.  There is no extinction droplet diameter reported because the droplet is in the HiBMS FOV for such a small fraction of the droplet lifetime.  It is unclear whether the droplet burned to completion of the flame extinguished at a finite droplet size, although given the ambient conditions and expected burning behavior, burnout is more likely.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm or nominally air ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE and out of the HiBMS FOV about 1/2 of the way through the burn.  The flame begins to oscillate and then drifts S and out of the LLUV FOV before extinction.  The Color camera IPSU did not record any images during the burn.  It is unclear whether the droplet continued to burn in the LLUV FOV and for how long.  The oscillations are significant, but the flame appears to be decreasing in size .  From the radiometer, it appears that the droplet burns with a stable flame after the flame oscillations stop.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with no translation in a 0.13/0.87 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  After deployment and ignition, there are significant axial oscillations along fiber axis throughout the burn.  The osciallations are significant and persistent.  The droplet remains within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  The droplet burns for a relatively long time in this low O2 ambient.  The flame was very dim and the LLUV flame size measurements are not reliable.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  After ignition the flame quickly extinguishes.  This is likely radiative extinction and it is quite possible this ambient condition is below the flammability limit for heptane.  The droplet has some unusual oscillations on the fiber during the burn that seem to disappear for most of the test (after the flame extinguishes).  The color camera IPSU did not record any images for this test.  There is a brief period of significant vaporization after visible flame extinction followed by formation of a small vapor cloud.  This is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction following visible flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N with a relatively high velocity in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, and out of the FOV shortly after ignition.  It appears that the droplet drifts close enough to the needle to start a needle fire that changes the droplet direction from N to E in the color camera FOV.  The droplet quickly leaves the color camera FOV while still burning.  The droplet remains in the LLUV FOV drifting S after deployment and ignition.  The needle fire is visible on the LLUV as well and it pushes the droplet N and out of the LLUV FOV before extinction or disruption.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There is almost no axial motion of the droplet relative to the fiber, but the droplet does oscillate radially on the fiber which causes minor disruptions in the flame and creates some scatter in the droplet history.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.86 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N and out of HiBMS FOV about 1/4th of the way through a very long burn that appeared to end in a diffusive extinction.  The droplet drifts E in the LLUV FOV and partially out of the FOV, but stays in the Color Camera FOV.  This was a very weak flame, barely visible on both the LLUV and color cameras.  There is no extinction droplet diameter reported because the droplet is only in the HiBMS FOV for a small fraction of the flame lifetime.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.82 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of the FOV 2/3rds of the through the test.  There is a small disruption near the end of the test.  Extrapolating the droplet history using the average burning rate constant shows a very small extinction droplet size, indicating the droplet burned essentially to completion.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.54/0.32 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NW in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition leaving the FOV just after visible flame extinction.  The flame oscillates several cycles with nearly constant amplitude before radiatively extinguishing.  The LLUV images are dim and the LLUV flame data is noisy as a result of the flame dimness and the contamination of the CIR LLUV viewing window.

Freely-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.30/0.80 O2/N2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NW out of the HiBMS FOV about half way through the burn.  The droplet appears to burn to completion or a very small size before a disruption that causes flame extinction.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/s translation burning in a 0.18/0.82 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet moves E in the HiBMS FOV with translation and continues to move E along the fiber and out of the FOV after the translation stops.  It also drifts partially out of the LLUV FOV.  The droplet then oscillates between the regions of the fiber where the flame impinges on it for several seconds before becoming quiescent and burning until, presumabley diffusive, flame extinction.  There was no apparent disruption at or near flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  This is a very large droplet that is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition.  The droplet eventually drifts S in the HiBMS FOV and leaves the FOV a short time before flame extinction.  The flame size from the color camera is a bit more reliable than the LLUV because of the very dim flame coupled with the contamination on the CIR LLUV viewing window.  The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating the droplet history from when the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until the time of flame extinction using the burning rate constant measured near the end of the time the droplet is within the HiBMS FOV.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.35 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and out of the FOV after visible flame extinction.  The droplet has a very low burning rate constant.  A relatively large vapor cloud forms well after visible flame extinction which indicates likely cool flame burning and extinction after visible flame extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.19/0.71/0.10 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition and just out of the FOV before flame extinction/disruption.  There may have been a disruption coincident with flame extinction.

Freely-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.30/0.70 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet remains in the FOV of all the cameras for the entire test.  The droplet drifts S, then E, then N in the HiBMS FOV.  Coincident with flame extinction, the droplet becomes almost 'football'-shaped.  The oblong shape with a pointed end remains stationary and fixed for several seconds (until recording ended).  The Dext is the actual extinction diameter, but may be influenced by the shape change.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.21/0.09/0.70 O2/N2/CO2, 3.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, hits the lower igniter and then drifts E and out of the HiBMS FOV very quickly.  The HiBMS and illumination settings were not correct, so the igniters obscure the droplet.  The background is also near saturation and the droplet size is a function of the 'quadrant slice' of the HiBMS image it is in.  The droplet drifts out of the LLUV FOV, but stays mostly in the color camera FOV.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.63/0.20 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet has almost no drift after deployment and ignition, moving slightly to the SE in the HiBMS FOV but remaining in the FOV of all the cameras for the entire test.  The color camera IPSU failed to record any images after deployment.  The flame extinguished after approximately 5 sec and that is likely followed by cool flame burning and extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The HiBMS IPSU did not record any images for this test.  The flame grew in size initially, got very dim, but then shranks, got brighter and burned to disruption at a small size.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with 3 mm/sec translation (for approximately 4 sec) burning in a 0.18/0.82 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The flame has moderate transverse oscillations and remains within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  The flame grows and becomes dim blue.  During translation, the leading edge of the flame is bright and the fiber glows brightly.  The trailing edge of the flame is much dimmer and the fiber does not glow.  After translation stops, the flame extinguishes.  There is significant droplet vaporization after visible flame extinction.  There is a small disruption very late in the droplet lifetime that leaves a small residual droplet on the fiber.  The behavior after visible flame extinction is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition.  It stops briefly at the corner of the FOV and then disappears from the FOV (there one frame, gone the next) at a time coincident with visible flame extinction.  The droplet may have  moved to just outside the FOV after the flame extinguished.  The droplet burned nicely to a diffusive extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter is the droplet diameter in the frame just before the droplet disappears.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  Almost no residual motion after deployment and ignition.  This is a relatively large droplet that stayed in the HiBMS FOV for the entire (short) burn and the entire recording time of the HiBMS IPSU.  The droplet radiatively extinguishes after a short burn with no flame oscillations.  There is significant post visible flame extinction vaporoization and large vapor cloud formed late in the recording time.  The post visible flame extinction behavior is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.55/0.30 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition.  It remains in the FOV for the duration of the burn, leaving shortly after visible flame extinction.  This ambient environment is likely near flammability boundary so it is difficult to determine whether it was diffusive or radiative extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NE after deployment and ignition, but remains in HiBMS FOV for duration of the burn and several seconds after flame extinction (long enough to observe the vaporization history).  The flame grows slightly reaches a maximum size 1/3rd of the way through the burn and then decreases in size in response to the shrinking droplet.  This is likely diffusive extinction, but very close to the flammability limit.  There is no evidence of a cool flame (rapid vaporization after visible flame extinction and no vapor cloud formation).

Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The HiBMS IPSU did not record any images for this test.  There were significant oscillations on fiber, so severe that the droplet became dislodged from the fiber and drifted S and out of the color camera FOV.  It also drifted out of the LLUV FOV.

Freely-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.30/0.70 O2/N2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition, leaving the FOV 1/2 through the burn before burning to near completion.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition.  It leaves the HiBMS FOV approximately 2/3rds of the way through the burn that ends with a diffusive extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter comes from extrapolating the droplet history until the time of extinction using the average burning rate constant from the last half of the time the droplet is within the HiBMS FOV.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.34/0.66 O2/N2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is almost motionless after deployment, but then a large impulse when the igniters start to heat moves droplet SW and quickly out of HiBMS FOV.  The droplet is nearly out of the FOV when the igniters begin to move away from the droplet.  There is significant sooting with large aggregates.  The data from this test are probably not reliable.

Free-floating heptane droplet in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NW and out of the HiBMS FOV before the end of the test (about half way).  After ignition, the droplet flame is luminous, quickly changing to a nearly all blue, dim flame.  The flame then begins to oscillate for several seconds before becoming stable and brighter and burning until a small disurption coincident with flame extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter is the droplet diameter when the flame disrupts and is estimated from the burning rate constant while the droplet is within the HiBMS FOV and the time of extinction from either the LLUV or color camera views.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.13/0.87 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  Very good deployment and ignition with almost no residual motion.  The droplet does drift S in the HiBMS and out of the FOV, but not until well after flame extinction.  This was a very dim flame.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.55/0.30 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There is a small amount of axial motion on the fiber, but it doesn't seem to influence the burning behavior to a large degree.  This is a relatively short, transient burn; likely radiative extincion.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with no translation in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There is a small droplet to the W of the main droplet that ignited and quickly burned off.  There is significant transverse and axial motion of the droplet on the fiber during most of the test.  The droplet drifted W on the fiber after deployment, but then stopped and oscillated (irregularly) axially and transversly during the entire burn.  There was a brief shape change from spherical at the time of the discrete change in droplet size that corresponded to something being ejected from the droplet (visible on the color camera view).

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  This is the first test after the needle and window change-out (cleaner window for the LLUV).  The droplet stays within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test with very little residual motion.  The LLUV image is very bright with none of the asymetry as observed in the previous tests.  The flame extinguishes at a relatively large droplet size and the droplet continuts to vaporize at a relatively high and nearly constant rate after visible flame extinction.  This is indicative of cool flame burning and extinction after visible-flame extinction.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  A smaller droplet that stays in the HiBMS FOV for the entiore test.  The droplet disrupts at a very small droplet size that is coincident with visible flame extinction.  The extinction droplet size is the droplet size just before the disruption.

Free-floating methanol droplet in a 0.21/0.49/0.30 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, hits the igniter then begins to drift slowly NW after ignition.  The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV before extinction, but most of the burning history is captured by the HiBMS.  The droplet burns for a long time before diffusive extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter is extrapolated fom the droplet size history from the time the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until visible flame extinction using the measured burning rate constant from the time period just before the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifted N after deployment and ignition and out of HiBMS FOV.  The droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV before disruptive flame extinction at a very small droplet size.  The extinction droplet diameter is the estimated droplet diameter (from extrapolating the droplet history until the disruption using the measured burning rate constant) when the disruption occurs.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/CO2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  This is a very short burn, radiative extinction with the flame extinguishing very quickly after translation starts.  Ther is no vapor cloud formation and the vaporization rate after visible flame extinction is quite small.  As a result, there is likely no, or only very brief, cool flame burning.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.12/0.88 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet deployed and ignited with almost no residual motion.  The droplet drifted a little S and then E in the HiBMS FOV, but remained in the FOV of the HiBMS, LLUV and color cameras for the entire recording time.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a0.30/0.70 O2/N2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet has some transverse oscillations after ignition.  The transverse oscillations diminish relatively quickly.  During and after translation the droplet oscillates axially.  It moves into and partially out of the HiBMS FOV (to the E).  The droplet stops moving both transversely and axially and burns smoothly eventually shrinking until it is fully in the HiBMS FOV.  Near the end of the test the droplet begins to oscillate on the fiber and disrupts, dislodging from the fiber and causing flame extinction.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet in a nominally air, 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There is some drift E on the fiber after ignition and early in the droplet lifetime.  The soot agglomerates that are near the droplet create a lot of noise in the droplet measurement for the first half of the burn.  There is a lot of motion of the droplet on the fiber late in the droplet lifetime as well.  There is evidence of some unusual soot dynamics with large soot particles moving slowly towards the droplet and then more rapidly pushed away (presumably by the Stefan flow).  The droplet burns to completion.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.42/0.40 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts N in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, then hits the igniter and drifts E and out of the FOV before extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter is extrapolated from the droplet history from the point the droplet leaves the HiBMS FOV until the time of visible flame extinction using the measured burning rate constant during the later period while the droplet is in the HiBMS FOV.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.34/0.66 O2/N2, 0.70 atm ambient environment. Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The flame oscillates for a few cycles (increasing in magnitude with time) until radiative extinction.  The flame is difficult to see with the LLUV because of both the dim flame and the contamination on the LLUV viewing window.

Free-floating heptane droplet in a 0.20/0.75/0.05 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in HiBMS and LLUV FOVs for the entire recording time.  The color camera IPUS did not record any images after deployment.  The flame radiatively extinguishes and there appears to be rapid vaporization followed by a plateau late in the recording time after the visible flame extinction.  This is indicative of cool flame and burning after visible flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.34/0.66 O2/N2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment and ignition.  It is in the HiBMS for only a short time, and also drifts quickly out of the Color Camera FOV.  It remains in the LLUV FOV for the entire burn and seems to burn to a very small extinction droplet size or completion.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.21/0.09/0.70 O2/N2/CO2, 2.0 atm ambient environment. There is 'hazing' around the droplet in the HiBMS view during combustion, almost like there is significant internal liquid motion.  The droplet disrupts after it drifts out of the HiBMS FOV. Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.15/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There was an error in the automated test sequence and the MDCA dispensed fuel before deployment. The droplet lifetime is very short with flame extinction occurring only a few seconds after igniter withdraw.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment. Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.30/0.70 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts S in the HiBMS FOV and leaves the FOV shortly after igniter withdraw.  There is a significant amount of sooting and a large soot shell surrounding the droplet.  The droplet drifts out of the color camera FOV, but starys in the LLUV FOV.  The droplet burns to disruption at a small size.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet burns for a long time before diffusive extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet deforms shortly after deployment, presumably due to a gas bubble that burst.  This causes the droplet to drift slowly NE in the HiBMS.  The droplet then had a large flash coincident with ignition that caused the droplet to drift SW at approximately 6 mm/sec. Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.18/0.67/0.15 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. The droplet then burns without axial or transverse motion until it disrupts and dislocated from the fiber coincident with flame extinction.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.19/0.71/0.10 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet has a pronounced drift S in the HiBMS FOV after deployment, strikes the igniter and continues to drift S and out of the HiBMS FOV about 1/3rd of the way through the burn.  The droplet burns for a relatively long time to a diffusive extinction.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images after deployment for this test.  There is no extinction droplet diameter listed for this test because of the short fraction of the total test the droplet was within the HiBMS FOV.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.15/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts SE and out of the HiBMS FOV, but then drifts back into the FOV a few seconds prior to flame extinction.  There is a droplet shape change with the apparent ejection of some material during ignition.  The droplet shape oscillates immediately after this.  The color camera IPSU did not record any images for this test.

Fiber-supported methanol droplet burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment. Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There was very little droplet motion after ignition.  Halfway through the burn, the droplet begins to drift E at approximately 3 mm/sec.  It drifts out of the HiBMS FOV just before flame extinction.  The extinction droplet diameter is extrapolated from the droplet history and the measured average burning rate constant just prior to the droplet leaving the HiBMS FOV.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.13/0.87 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NW in the HiBMS FOV and out of the FOV about half way through the test.  The flame stays within the LLUV and color camera FOVs for the entire test.  The extinction droplet diameter is based on extrapolating the droplet history using the known burning rate constant from droplet history just prior to the droplet leaving the HiBMS FOV.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.14/0.51/0.35 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet is nearly motionless after deployment and ignition in the HiBMS FOV.  It starts to drift S as it burns and leaves the FOV well after visible flame extinction.  The droplet burns for only a very short time and the flame is very dim, almost undetectable in both the LLUV and Color Cameras.  The droplet is very near or even below the flammability limit.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.18/0.82 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. There is continued rapid vaporization after visible flame extinction and the formation of a large vapor cloud. Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a nominally air, 0.21/0.79 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment. Fiber-supported methanol droplet with 3 mm/sec translation burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  There is not much axial oscillatory motion associated with fiber motion but some transverse oscillations.  The droplet disrupts right around the time of extinction. Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.80 O2/N2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts E after ignition and leaves the HiBMS FOV shortly after visible flame extinction.  The droplet the re-enters the HiBMS FOV from the E a few seconds prior to the stop of video recording.  There is vapor cloud formation in the color camera view approximately 20 sec after visible flame extinction.  It is not clear whether cool flame burning and extinction occurred for this test.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts E, but stays in HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  The droplet burns linearly to small size and there is disruption coincident with flame extinction.  The extinction droplet size is just an extrapolation of the average burning rate to the time of extinction.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.15/0.85 O2/N2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  There are significant oscillation on the fiber after deployment that persist throughout the burn.  The oscillations cause the droplet to become misshapen and cause large errors/scatter in the droplet size measurement.  This is a very short burn and although there is not a large disruption, the oscillations compromise the data from the test.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.16/0.59/0.25 O2/N2/He, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The HiBMS IPSU did not record any images for this test.  There was only a very small drift S in color camera FOV, but stays in FOV for entire test (as well as the LLUV FOV).  The droplet burned to extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.23/0.52/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts slowly E in the HiBMS FOV, but stays within the HiBMS FOV for the entire recording time (including post-extinction).  There is some rapid post-extinction vaporization, but not as pronounced as other heptane tests, followed by a plateau in the droplet history.  The flame radiatively extinguishes, and is likely followed by a cool flame and cool flame extinction.  The Color Camera IPSU-4 failed to record any images after deployment.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.19/0.71/0.10 O2/N2/CO2, 0.7 atm ambient environment.  The droplet stays in HiBMS FOV for the entire test including after the visible flame extinction.  The flame has a radiative extinction followed by rapid vaporization and then a plateau late in the test time.  The plateau is coincident with vapor cloud formation.  Both the post visible-flame extinction behavior and plateau in the droplet history are indicative of cool flame burning and extinction, respectively.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a cabin air (nominally 0.21/0.79 O2/N2), 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet deploys and ignites with little residual velocity and stays within the HiBMS FOV for the entire test.  The droplet burns with a very luminous flame that obscures droplet in HiBMS for a large portion of the test.  The droplet burns to disruption at a small droplet size with the last part of the droplet history obscured by the luminous flame.

Free-floating methanol droplet burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient evnironment.  The droplet stays in the FOV of all cameras after deployment and ignition.  The flame oscillates for one or two cycles before radiatively extinguishing.  This condition is very near, if not over, the flammability limit.  The Color Camera flame size data is a bit more reliable than the LLUV which had a lot of noise and a flame that was barely distinguishable from the background.

Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.17/0.38/0.45 O2/N2/He, 0.70 atm ambient environment.  The droplet exhibits significant axial and radial oscillations throughout the test.  The burning rate and extinction diameter data are strongly influenced by this motion.  The residual droplet on the fiber has a large gas bubble that results in the size jump after visible flame extinction.

Free-floating heptane droplet burning in a 0.24/0.56/0.20 O2/N2/CO2, 1.0 atm ambient environment.  The droplet drifts NW and out of the HiBMS FOV about half way through the test.  After deployment, there is a disruption (maybe a bubble burst since these droplets had issues with gas bubbles) that causes significant droplet deformation and oscillations.  There is a moderate degree of sooting.  The droplet burns to a relatively small size before disruptive extinction.  The noise in the beginning of the droplet history is due to soot influencing the droplet size measurement.  The color camera IPSU failed to record any images after deployment.  The LLUV IPSU stopped recording images for a brief time in the middle of the burn.
